knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: software generation plan
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes generating and checking Poisson and Exponential simulated values?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the generation and sanity-check procedure.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Simulation requires both generation and basic validation against support and moments. Software output alone or a mean-only check is insufficient.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson: non-negative integers and mean check. Exponential: positive values and mean check.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Generating values without checking support and whether simple sample summaries are plausible.

choices.label: Generate Poisson values with the chosen mean parameter and check that values are non-negative integers with sample mean near that parameter. Generate Exponential values with the chosen mean and check positivity and a sample mean near that mean.
Generate both distributions and accept the output without checking support or sample summaries because a library sampler cannot fail.
Check Poisson values are positive real numbers and Exponential values are non-negative integers, since both use a mean parameter.
A matching sample mean proves the simulated distribution is correct even if Poisson outputs are fractional or Exponential outputs are negative.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: refuse Chapter 2 complete
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You simulate Poisson(λ=3) counts and Exponential waiting times with mean 2. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Choose the valid simulation and sanity-check conclusion.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The checks must match each distribution's support and mean. A sampler performs generation, not validation or a substitute for inverse-transform understanding.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson: integers near mean 3. Exponential: positive near mean 2. Sampler does not replace inverse-transform understanding or sanity checks.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating software generation as complete without support or mean checks, or equating a sampler with inverse-transform understanding.

choices.label: Poisson draws should be non-negative integers with sample mean near 3. Exponential draws should be positive with sample mean near 2. A built-in sampler does not replace understanding inverse-transform sampling, and generating alone is not a completed sanity check.
Using a built-in sampler removes the need to inspect support or sample means because software generation is itself a sanity check.
Poisson draws should average near 2 and Exponential draws near 3 because λ is a waiting-time mean.
The simulation is valid if both samples contain only integers, since Exponential waiting times are discrete event counts.

worked_example.title: Generate and sanity-check Poisson and Exponential draws
worked_example.problem_statement: An analyst needs software samples from two univariate families before any joint modelling: (i) annual claim counts as Poisson(λ = 3); (ii) inter-claim waiting times (days) as Exponential with mean θ = 5. Describe the generation plan for n = 50 draws of each family, state one sanity check for each sample, and decide whether a mean of 3.1 on the Poisson sample alone proves the software call was correct.

given.note: illustrative software output for the refuse step

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Name a sampler for each family, one check against support or mean, then judge whether 3.1 alone certifies the Poisson call.

steps.label: Plan the two software samplers
steps.attempt_cue: Name a discrete call for Poisson(3) and a continuous call for Exponential mean 5.
steps.explanation: Software generation starts from a named family and parameter, not from a blank RNG. Poisson uses a discrete count sampler; Exponential uses a positive continuous sampler with mean 5 (or rate 1/5, depending on the package convention).
steps.calculation: Poisson: rpois / Poisson(3); Exponential: rexp(mean=5) or Exp(rate=0.2)
steps.result: Two named samplers, parameters fixed before drawing

steps.label: Run one sanity check per sample
steps.attempt_cue: State a support check and a rough mean check.
steps.explanation: A usable check compares sample behaviour with the family's support and first moment. Poisson draws must be non-negative integers with sample mean near 3; Exponential draws must be strictly positive with sample mean near 5.
steps.calculation: Poisson: all ≥ 0 integers, mean ≈ 3; Exponential: all > 0, mean ≈ 5
steps.result: Support + rough mean check for each family

steps.label: Refuse mean-near-target as sole proof
steps.attempt_cue: Decide whether sample mean 3.1 alone proves the Poisson call was correct.
steps.explanation: A sample mean near λ is consistent with Poisson(3) but does not by itself prove the call, the seed, or the parameterisation. Generation without a support/parameter check, and without refusing overclaim that univariate sampling finishes joint work, is incomplete.
steps.calculation: 3.1 ≈ 3 is consistent, not a proof of correct generation
steps.result: Mean proximity alone does not certify the sampler

worked_example.final_answer: Generate n = 50 from Poisson(3) and Exponential(mean 5) with named software samplers; check support and rough means; a Poisson sample mean of 3.1 is consistent but not sole proof that the call was correct.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating any code that prints numbers as generation complete, or treating a sample mean near 3 as proof the Poisson(3) call was correct without checking support, parameterisation, or that joint distributions remain out of scope.
